learn.title: Ratios in right triangles
learn.body: In similar right triangles with the same acute angle, the ratios of sides are the same whatever the size. Those ratios get names. They are the start of trigonometry.

learn.title: Naming the sides
learn.body: Pick an acute angle $A$. The hypotenuse is the longest side. The opposite side faces $A$. The adjacent side touches $A$ and is not the hypotenuse. The sides change names if you pick the other acute angle.
learn.alt: A right triangle with angle A at the bottom right corner. The vertical side is marked opposite A, the horizontal side adjacent to A, and the slanted side hypotenuse.

learn.title: The three ratios
learn.body: $\sin A=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$, $\cos A=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$, $\tan A=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$. Many people remember them as SOH, CAH, TOA.

learn.title: Compute the ratios
learn.body: A right triangle has sides $3,4,5$. Angle $A$ is opposite the side of length 3.
Handy values: $\sin30^\circ=\frac12$, $\cos60^\circ=\frac12$, $\tan45^\circ=1$. These come from the special triangles.

questions.explanation: SOH: sine is opposite over hypotenuse.
TOA: tangent is opposite over adjacent.

questions.prompt: A right triangle has sides $5,12,13$. Angle $A$ is opposite the side of length 5. Find $\tan A$ as a fraction.
In a $3,4,5$ triangle, angle $A$ is opposite the side 3. Find $\cos A$ as a decimal.

questions.explanation: In a 30-60-90 triangle the side opposite $30^\circ$ is half the hypotenuse.
In a 45-45-90 triangle the legs are equal, so opposite over adjacent is 1.

questions.prompt: Match each ratio to its meaning.
